# Results — Study 630 (Late Filers, Form NT)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — **a company
that cannot file its 10-K/10-Q on time (an EDGAR NT 10-K / NT 10-Q filing under Rule 12b-25) is
telling you something: sell** — tested as a market-adjusted event study on every NT filing on
EDGAR that maps to a currently-listed ticker, 2004-01 → 2026-03. Short at the close of the day
after the filing (exactly ONE execution lag), hold 60 trading days, benchmark SPY. Offline &
deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of
**2026-06-30** (last complete month; events end 2026-03-31 so every 60-trading-day window is
complete). Fingerprints: events `82ef3cc79145`, SPY `860d1267b8a2`.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| NT filing index | EDGAR quarterly form-type master index, 2002Q1 → 2026Q2: **102,505** exact-form NT filings (**37,502** NT 10-K / **65,003** NT 10-Q) |
| Event window | 2004-01-01 → 2026-03-31: **89,497** filings; **17,199 (19.2%)** map to a **currently-registered** ticker (`company_tickers.json`) |
| Panel (seeded caps, stated) | 500-ticker / 2,000-event caps → **1,993** events on **421** tickers |
| Usable events | **1,180** after the stated screens — entry price ≥ **$1** (sub-$1 pinks are unshortable and carry the worst Yahoo adjustment glitches), no \|daily move\| > 100% in-window, ≥ 80% coverage. 494 NT 10-K / 686 NT 10-Q; 822 repeat offenders |
| Prices | yfinance daily auto-adjusted (total-return) closes, **5,807 days × 422 names**, 2003-06-02 → 2026-06-30 |
| Execution / costs | filing lands day 0 (often after hours) → **short at the close of day +1**; CAR = Σ daily (stock − SPY), days +2…+61; short pays **2 × one-way cost + borrow × 60/252** |

> **Survivorship (named on the Signal axis — and unusually severe here).** Only **19.2%** of NT
> filings map to a currently-registered ticker: the CIK→ticker registry covers **survivors
> only**. Chronic late filers delist at high rates, and the claim's very teeth — the frauds and
> bankruptcies that followed an NT — *end in delisting*, so they cannot enter this panel. The
> $1 entry floor further removes the most distressed names. Every drift number below is
> therefore biased **toward zero**: this tape measures the NT signal on the survivors, i.e. its
> *mildest* corner. We say so out loud rather than pretend coverage we don't have.

## The announcement (context, NOT tradable)

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| reaction, filing day → entry close | **−33.0 bps** (naive *t* = −0.99, n = 1,180) |

The confession itself barely moves these (survivor) names — most panel NTs are routine
extensions by chronic laggards, and the catastrophic ones happened off-panel.

## The post-filing drift — the tested rule

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| mean CAR[+1, +60td] vs SPY | **−105.7 bps** per event |
| naive cross-sectional *t* (windows overlap → over-counted; reported, not relied on) | −0.71 |
| **calendar-time portfolio (PRIMARY)** | **+3.39 bps/day** vs SPY, **HAC *t* = +0.83** (+8.9%/yr; 5,623 active days, avg 12.6 names/day) |

The primary test cannot tell the post-NT window from noise — the sign even flips between the
per-event mean (−106 bps) and the calendar-time daily mean (+3.4 bps/day), which is what "no
signal on this tape" looks like on a wide-tailed small-cap panel.

## Controls

| control | mean CAR | test |
|---|--:|--|
| real NT events | −105.7 bps (n = 1,180) | — |
| same firms, 252 td earlier (NT-free windows) | +81.9 bps (n = 714) | Welch *t* events-vs-pseudo = **−0.77** |
| random dates × **25 seeds** (house rule: no single-seed baselines) | +381.2 bps (σ across seeds 147.1) | events sit *below* the names' own baseline drift, but not significantly |

The survivor panel drifts *up* on random dates (that is what surviving to 2026 looks like);
NT windows sit ~490 bps below that baseline — the right *sign* for the claim, but Welch
*t* = −0.77 is noise, not evidence.

No slice and no horizon clears (or approaches) the bar.

## Third axis — is the SECOND consecutive NT the real kill signal?

| group | CAR (bps) | n | cal-time HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| repeat offenders (prior NT ≤ 15 months) | **+58.0** | 822 | +1.18 |
| first offenses | **−481.7** | 358 | −0.59 |

Repeat − first = **+539.7 bps**, Welch *t* = **+1.85**. The folklore is **BUSTED** on this
tape: the second (third, tenth…) NT is, if anything, *milder* than the first — chronic
lateness gets priced as routine, and the difference is the *wrong sign* for the "second NT
kills" rule (and still sub-2 anyway).

## Tradability — the short pays twice, then pays the borrow

Gross short capture = +105.7 bps per event (60-td hold); net after 2 × one-way cost + borrow:

| one-way cost | borrow %/yr | net (bps/event) |
|--:|--:|--:|
| 10 bps | 3% | **+14.3** |
| 10 bps | 10% | **−152.4** |
| 20 bps | 3% | **−5.7** |
| 20 bps | 10% | **−172.4** |

Even *granting* the (uncertified) gross drift, the short nets ≈ zero at large-cap costs and
goes firmly negative at realistic small-cap borrow — and NT filers are precisely the
hard-to-borrow kind. The fattest historical payoffs (shorts that went to zero) sit in delisted
names that are missing from the panel *and* were the hardest to locate borrow on. **Mirage.**

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful

Deterministic beta-1 panel, planted NT-style events, TUNABLE post-event drift:

| planted drift | CAR (bps) | naive *t* | cal-time HAC *t* |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 0 bps/day (null) | +90.6 | +0.94 | **+0.55** |
| −20 bps/day | −1,152.3 | −11.93 | **−10.42** |

With nothing planted the machinery stays silent; with a −20 bps/day drift planted over the
measured window it lights up at HAC *t* = −10.4. The real-tape non-result is not a power
failure of the harness. *(Machinery proof only — never cited as market evidence.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** The literature (Alford-Jones-Zmijewski 1994; Griffin 2003; Bartov et al.;
  Duarte-Silva et al. 2013) documents negative post-NT abnormal returns — but **this tape
  cannot certify it**: calendar-time HAC *t* = **+0.83**, matched self-control Welch
  *t* = **−0.77**, no slice or horizon near 2. The panel is **severely survivor-biased**
  (only 19.2% of NT filings map to a live ticker; the delisting disasters that give the claim
  its teeth are structurally excluded), which biases the measured drift toward zero — so we
  read "literature says real; this survivors-only tape alone can't certify it" and stamp WEAK,
  not NONE.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Net short edge ≈ +14 bps/event in the *most* generous cost case and
  negative everywhere else; the names that would carry the edge are small, hard-to-borrow or
  already delisted. Beta, borrow and accessibility eat it.
- **"Second consecutive NT is the kill signal"? — BUSTED.** Repeat offenders drift *milder*
  than first offenses (+58 vs −482 bps; Welch *t* = +1.85, wrong sign for the folklore). The
  first confession — not the second — is where whatever information exists lives.
